item.title: Death toll at Iranian girls' school rises to 148
item.description:
A missile strike on a girls' elementary school in the southern Iranian city of Minab emerged as the deadliest single incident of the joint U.S.-Israeli military operation against Iran, with the death toll climbing from an initial count of 108 reported by the Iranian Red Crescent to 148 according to the local prosecutor, as cited by Iranian state media and confirmed by The Wall Street Journal and CNN.

The strike hit the Shajareh Tayyebeh all-girls primary school at approximately 10:45 a.m. local time on Saturday, February 28, as roughly 170 students between the ages of seven and 12 were attending class during what is a regular school day in Iran. The impact destroyed the building's walls and caused its roof to collapse, burying students underneath the rubble. Verified footage showed thick black smoke rising from a structure adorned with pastel-painted flowers, as rescuers used cranes and shovels to reach those trapped inside.

item.title: Iran's foreign minister vows 'no limit' to self-defense after Khamenei killed
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared on Sunday that Iran sees "no limit" to its right to self-defense following the assassination of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in coordinated US-Israeli strikes, rejecting President Donald Trump's warnings against retaliation and framing the military response as a matter of national survival.

item.title: ESA releases new images of interstellar comet ahead of Jupiter flyby
item.description:
The interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS, the third object ever confirmed to have entered our solar system from beyond, is heading for a close encounter with Jupiter on March 16, when it will pass within 33 million miles of the gas giant. The flyby marks one of the final observable milestones before the ancient visitor disappears into the void of interstellar space.

First detected in July 2025 by a NASA-funded ATLAS telescope in Chile, the comet has captivated astronomers with its extraordinary speed — clocked at 137,000 miles per hour — and a hyperbolic trajectory confirming it could not have originated in our solar system. Only two interstellar objects had previously been identified: 1I/'Oumuamua in 2017 and 2I/Borisov in 2019.

item.title: Trump says he agreed to talk with Iran as strikes continue
item.description: The United States and Israel launched a massive joint military operation against Iran on February 28, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and dozens of senior military and political leaders in what the Pentagon dubbed "Operation Epic Fury" and Israel codenamed "Roaring Lion." Iran responded with retaliatory missile and drone strikes across the Middle East, targeting Israel and U.S. military bases in at least six countries, killing three American service members and raising fears of a wider regional war.

item.title: Major shipping firms halt Suez Canal transit after strikes on Iran
item.description:
A.P. Moller-Maersk announced on Sunday that it will halt all sailings through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Suez Canal, rerouting vessels around the Cape of Good Hope after U.S. and Israeli military strikes on Iran plunged the region's key maritime chokepoints into crisis. The decision reverses the Danish shipping giant's recent move to resume transit through the Red Sea corridor, which had been disrupted by Houthi rebel attacks since late 2023.

"Due to the deteriorating security situation in the Middle East region following the escalating military conflict, we have decided to pause future Trans-Suez sailings through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait for the time being," Maersk said in a statement.

item.title: Trump says Iran war could last four weeks as combat operations intensify
item.description:
President Donald Trump declared on Sunday that U.S. military operations in Iran will continue "in full force" until all American objectives are met, as the joint U.S.-Israeli campaign entered its second day with mounting casualties on all sides and retaliatory strikes reverberating across the Middle East.

In a video posted to Truth Social, Trump acknowledged the deaths of three American service members and warned that more losses are likely. "Combat operations continue at this time in full force, and they will continue until all of our objectives are achieved," he said, pledging to "avenge" the fallen troops. In a phone interview with the Daily Mail, Trump offered the clearest timeline yet for the campaign, saying, "It's always been a four-week process. We figured it will be four weeks or so. It's a big country. It'll take four weeks — or less".

item.title: Trump confirms three US troops killed as he warns more may follow
item.description:
President Donald Trump acknowledged Sunday that three American service members had been killed during the U.S.-Israeli military offensive against Iran and warned that more casualties were likely as combat operations continue. "We have three casualties, but we expect more; ultimately, this will lead to a significant outcome for the world," Trump told NBC News.

The deaths, announced by U.S. Central Command at 9:30 a.m. ET on March 1, mark the first confirmed American fatalities since the joint operation — dubbed Operation Epic Fury — began early Saturday. Five additional service members were seriously wounded, while several others sustained minor shrapnel injuries and concussions and were returning to duty, CENTCOM said in a post on X.

item.title: Canada's Carney arrives in Delhi for Modi talks amid Iran crisis
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney landed in New Delhi on Saturday as part of a three-nation tour aimed at deepening trade ties with Indo-Pacific partners, even as U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran and Tehran's retaliatory attacks across the Middle East cast a shadow over global diplomacy.

item.title: BOJ deputy governor says rate hikes to continue
item.description:
Bank of Japan Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino said Monday that the central bank should continue raising interest rates as it moves toward a more neutral monetary policy, reinforcing expectations that further tightening lies ahead even as the Japanese economy sends mixed signals.

"While the Bank's policy remains somewhat accommodative, it should gradually shift to a more neutral stance through moderate policy rate hikes," Himino said in a speech to local business leaders in Wakayama.

item.title: Melania Trump to chair UN Security Council amid US war on Iran
item.description:
First Lady Melania Trump is scheduled to preside over a United Nations Security Council meeting on Monday afternoon, an unprecedented appearance that was planned weeks ago but now collides with the reality of active US military operations in Iran.

The session, titled "Children, Technology, and Education in Conflict," will mark the first time a sitting US First Lady has chaired the 15-member council, according to UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric. The meeting comes as the United States assumes the rotating presidency of the Security Council for March.

item.title: Factory growth accelerates across Indonesia, India, Thailand in February
item.description: Factory activity across three of Southeast and South Asia's largest economies gained momentum in February, with purchasing managers' index data released Monday by S&P Global showing accelerating expansion in Indonesia, India, and Thailand, driven by strengthening domestic demand and rising new orders.

item.title: Iran fires missiles at Israel and US sites across Gulf in retaliation
item.description:
Iran launched a sweeping wave of missile and drone attacks against Israel and U.S. military installations across the Persian Gulf over the weekend, striking targets in at least eight countries in retaliation for a joint U.S.-Israeli military operation that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Saturday.

The Iranian offensive, which began hours after coordinated American and Israeli strikes hit Tehran and other Iranian cities on February 28, has killed at least nine Israelis in a single ballistic missile strike on Beit Shemesh, three U.S. service members, and several others across the Gulf region, while injuring hundreds and paralyzing air travel across the Middle East.

item.title: Israel strikes Beirut after Hezbollah shatters ceasefire with rocket attack
item.description:
Israel launched its most intensive airstrikes on Beirut since the 2024 war early Monday, pounding Hezbollah-controlled southern suburbs of the Lebanese capital after the Iran-backed group fired rockets and drones at northern Israel for the first time since a U.S.-brokered ceasefire took effect in November 2024. More than a dozen explosions rocked Beirut beginning around 2:40 a.m. local time, sending residents fleeing on foot and by car and clogging roads out of the city.

The exchange marks a dramatic widening of the conflict that erupted over the weekend when the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

item.title: Iran's top security chief rejects talks with US as strikes enter third day
item.description:
Ali Larijani, the head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, declared on Monday that Tehran "will not negotiate with the United States," flatly rejecting claims that Iranian officials had sought to restart talks with Washington. The statement, posted on X, came hours after President Donald Trump told The Atlantic that Iran's new leadership wanted dialogue and that he had "agreed to talk".

Larijani's rebuke marks a sharp public break with the diplomatic track Trump floated over the weekend, even as US and Israeli strikes on Iran entered their third day following the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Saturday.

item.title: AWS outage spreads to Bahrain as Gulf strikes continue
item.description:
Amazon Web Services suffered a major disruption to its cloud infrastructure in the United Arab Emirates after unidentified objects struck one of its data centers on Sunday, sparking a fire that forced an extended power shutdown as Iranian retaliatory strikes battered the Gulf region.

AWS confirmed on its status page that at approximately 4:30 a.m. PST on March 1, its Availability Zone mec1-az2 in the ME-CENTRAL-1 Region "was impacted by objects that struck the data center, creating sparks and fire". The fire department cut power to the entire facility, including backup generators, while crews worked to extinguish the blaze. The company did not confirm or deny whether the incident was connected to the Iranian strikes when asked by Reuters.

item.title: Satellite images show smoke over Dubai as Iran's Gulf strikes enter third day
item.description: Satellite imagery captured on March 1 has revealed thick plumes of black smoke rising over Dubai's skyline, offering stark visual evidence of the damage caused by Iran's ongoing retaliatory missile and drone attacks across the Persian Gulf region. The before-and-after images — comparing clear skies on February 24 with smoke columns and burn marks days later — underscore how quickly the conflict between the United States and Iran has reached the doorstep of the Gulf's most prominent commercial hub.

item.title: NOAA sees up to 60% chance El Nino forms later in 2026
item.description:
The El Niño weather phenomenon could develop later this year, potentially pushing global temperatures to new record heights, according to the latest forecasts from U.S. and international climate agencies.

NOAA's Climate Prediction Center estimates a 50 to 60 percent chance that El Niño will form during the July-to-September period and beyond. The World Meteorological Organization is expected to issue an update on El Niño on Tuesday.

item.title: India's factory growth hits 4-month high as UK, Australia slow
item.description: Manufacturing activity across major economies showed diverging trends in February 2026, with Australia and the United Kingdom losing steam even as India's factory sector accelerated to a four-month high, according to purchasing managers' index data released this week by S&P Global.

item.title: Three US F-15s shot down by Kuwaiti air defenses in friendly fire incident
item.description:
Three US Air Force F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jets crashed in Kuwait on Monday morning after being mistakenly shot down by Kuwaiti air defenses during active combat operations against Iran, the US Central Command confirmed.

All six crew members ejected safely and are in stable condition after being recovered and transported to hospitals, CENTCOM said in a statement. The incident marks the first loss of American aircraft in the four-day-old conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran.

item.title: Claude AI hit by worldwide outage across all platforms
item.description:
Anthropic's Claude AI chatbot went down on Monday in a worldwide outage that left users unable to access the platform across its web interface, mobile apps, and developer API.

The company flagged the incident on its status page at 11:49 UTC on March 2, 2026, posting an initial "Investigating" notice, followed by an update at 12:06 UTC stating the investigation was ongoing. Users attempting to reach the service reported failed requests, timeouts, and error messages including "This isn't working right now" and upstream connection termination errors.
